fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x1CAF3C0 (AddImmediateDefault, ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw size 0xC) writes the byte *puVar4 = 1 and an 8-byte zero at +4; macOS default ctor stores w=1 at +0. Live (5 instances, fight/idle): low byte always 01, bytes 1..3 vary (0 or garbage 0x85/0x2C/0xAA) - so only one byte is meaningful. Probably an 'update enabled' flag; no reader decoded.

fields.name: _Pad1
fields.evidence: Alignment padding before the float at +4; live bytes there are uninitialised garbage in one instance.

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: Default 0 (bg3.exe+0x1CAF3C0, macOS stp wzr,wzr,[x23,#4]). Live floats 0, 0.008125, 0.1667 (1/6), 0.2 - looks like an update interval in seconds.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: Default 0. Live takes the same set of values as +4 (0 .. 0.2); probably the accumulated time / time until next update paired with field_4.

open_questions: Meaning of the byte at +0 and of the two floats: the component is only reached through queries (Character + PathingComponent + Transform + Level, with CharacterOutOfSightFadeActiveView0, see bg3.exe+0x1CB3C90 / 0x1CB4480); the Toolkit has no named ecl::CharacterManager::Update body to read.
Whether +4/+8 are interval and timer or the other way round.
